SSC3-J1b A/B, 10 ALTERNATING pairs, same binary, --no-specialize as the OFF arm. NO EFFECT, in either direction: "on" was faster in 5 of 10 pairs, and the 15.5 ms median difference is a third of the 42.7 ms pooled sd. Within-arm spread 2.41x (on) and 2.17x (off) at host load 45-54, so the ratio column here is noise and must NOT be quoted as a 13% regression. Load-independent reason, from javap: binI64 is 895 bytecodes and binF64 578, both far over FreqInlineSize=325, so neither is inlined into step -- which is itself 5918 and never inlined into exec. The fast path swaps a tuple match for a call and leaves the per-op Value.VInt allocation alone. Evidence points at J0, not at shrinking binI64.

SSC3-J2 closure lane, 8 alternating pairs, one binary, --closures against the default. 1 of 8 pairs -- SIGNIFICANT IN THE DIRECTION OPPOSITE TO THE ONE INTENDED (sign test p ~ 0.035). The closure lane is SLOWER. MECHANISM: J0c already inlined step (236 bytes) into exec and its match over a sealed Instr is a tableswitch -- one hot predicted path. The closure lane replaces it with ops(i)(regs), a MEGAMORPHIC call site HotSpot cannot inline. The optimization was designed against a baseline that no longer existed. Lane kept behind --closures for its DIFFERENTIAL value, not its speed.
